title: adaptive-fidelity-market-experiments-roadmap-2028-q1
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview:

This roadmap describes a coordinated program of market-facing experiments and internal simulations to validate adaptive fidelity bundles (high/medium/low output fidelity) combined with dynamic pricing and onboarding flows. The goal is to identify product-configurations that maximize net revenue per request while maintaining customer-visible SLOs for latency and quality. This is a product + go-to-market initiative with heavy engineering support (Optimize + Serving Runtime + Console).

Goals:
- Establish 3 fidelity tiers (High, Medium, Low) with clear cost-to-quality tradeoffs and price points for hosted and dedicated customers.
- Prove a neutral-to-positive overall revenue impact (net revenue per token) for at least two customer segments within 12 weeks of experiment start.
- Keep customer-facing SLOs: p95 latency <= 250ms and quality regressions < 1.5% (measured by eval prompt sets) per route.
- Define rollout criteria and automation for per-route fidelity recommendations in Redwood Console.

Hypotheses to validate (examples):
1) Many customers will accept a Medium fidelity default for background tasks if price is ~30% lower and latency improves 10–20%.
2) For chat/interactive routes, a "smart fallback" that reduces fidelity only when p99 latency >400ms will improve availability without measurable quality loss.
3) A meterable fidelity credit (small upfront credit applied to Medium/Low) will increase adoption without materially increasing churn.

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: Hosted API customers (self-serve + SMB sales-assisted) and Dedicated customers with opt-in via Console. Private on-prem deployments are excluded from initial experiments.
- Constraint: Experiments must not violate enterprise customers’ pinned-variant constraints; enterprise routes that explicitly pin model variants will be excluded.
- Data handling: All A/B data and logs will follow existing telemetry and privacy policies; no customer user data leaves the platform for analysis except aggregated metrics.

Definitions (for this program):
- Fidelity tiers:
  - High: full-precision variants (FP16/AMP, no aggressive quantization), highest output consistency. Target use: core chat, compliance-sensitive outputs.
  - Medium: optimized kernels + int8/4 quantization with tuned temperature/profile. Lower cost, slightly higher variance. Target: background summarization, search snippets.
  - Low: aggressive quantization (int4 / 3-bit profiles), energy-optimized kernels. Target: bulk embedding-like tasks where latency matters more than nuance.

Success metrics (quantitative):
- Primary: Net revenue per 1M tokens served (USD), measured weekly, segmented by customer cohort.
- Secondary: 1) p95 request latency across routes; 2) eval-set quality delta per route (population-weighted); 3) Adoption rate of Medium/Low across eligible routes; 4) Change in churn rate for test cohorts.

Experiment pillars and milestones (12-week cadence):
1) Simulation and off-line modeling (Weeks 0–3)
   - Run high-fidelity cost/latency simulator with representative workload traces (samples from June–Oct 2027).
   - Parameters: batch size distribution, sequence length percentiles (P50/P90/P99), kv-cache hit rates.
   - Deliverable: Simulation report with expected per-token cost delta and p95/p99 latency projections for each fidelity tier.

2) Internal pilot (Weeks 3–6)
   - Select 3 internal product routes and 5 partner customers (opt-in) for closed beta.
   - Implement per-route fidelity controls and Console UI to toggle defaults.
   - Run canary traffic at 5% for 2 weeks, monitor latency, errors, and eval divergence.
   - Deliverable: Pilot post-mortem with recommended price points.

3) Public A/B experiment (Weeks 6–12)
   - Roll out to a randomized subset of self-serve customers grouped by profile (startup, midmarket, infra teams).
   - Experiment arms: Control (no change), Medium-default (price -30%), Smart-fallback (High default with fidelity reduction on pressure).
   - Monitor: SLOs, quality deltas, revenue, adoption.
   - Deliverable: Decision memo recommending 0/1 scale decisions (deploy, iterate, or rollback).

Rollout criteria and decision gates:
- Safety gate (pre-A/B): Simulation must show p95 latency within 10% of baseline for each candidate route under expected load.
- Quality gate: Eval-set regression for any route must be < 1.5% (absolute) for Medium tier in the pilot.
- Revenue gate: Expected net revenue per 1M tokens must increase or be neutral for at least one target cohort in simulation.

Console UX and API changes (summary):
- New per-route fidelity default control with three radio options (High/Medium/Low).
- New global account-level preference to express cost-sensitivity (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive).
- Telemetry: additional fields in usage events: fidelity_tier, simulated_cost_saved_usd, fidelity_reason (default|fallback|user_override).
- API: PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id} body will accept "default_fidelity": "high|medium|low". Example:

  PATCH /v1/routes/abc123
  Content-Type: application/json

  {
    "default_fidelity": "medium"
  }


Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customers perceive fidelity downgrades as quality regressions.
  Mitigation: Conservative defaults, clear Console messaging, 2-week opt-out grace, and fine-grained route-level opt-out.
- Risk: Unexpected p99 latency regressions on long-sequence requests when using aggressive quantization.
  Mitigation: Smart-fallback rules (detect rising p99 and switch to higher fidelity variant), automated rollback on SLO breach.
- Risk: Billing edge cases and disputes.
  Mitigation: Pre-release billing FAQ and small credit applied to initial adoption cohorts; finance-legal to provide T&Cs update.

Data and metrics instrumentation (required dashboards):
- Per-fidelity tier: cost-per-token estimate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, eval-quality-delta.
- Route-level adoption metrics: percent routes with Medium/Low default, top 50 routes by volume that chose Medium/Low.
- Cohort revenue dashboard: segmented by company size and industry vertical.

Appendix A — Simulation parameter table (example):

| Parameter | Baseline | Medium | Low | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Average per-token cost (USD) | 0.0016 | 0.00112 (-30%) | 0.0008 (-50%) | Kernel & quantization assumptions
| p95 latency (ms) | 240 | 200 (-17%) | 170 (-29%) | Measured on sample traces; p99 will be monitored
| Eval-quality delta (relative) | 0.0 | -0.8% | -2.4% | Weighted on conversational eval set

Appendix B — Example acceptance checklist for pilot routes:
1) Route has automated eval set integrated into CI (yes/no).
2) Baseline telemetry available for 30 days (yes/no).
3) Customer route owner opt-in confirmed (yes/no).
4) Billing credit applied and visible in Console (yes/no).
5) Rollback policy configured and tested (yes/no).
